newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mbeki says next talks last chance for Zaire peace.
newsitem.headline: Mbeki says next talks last chance for Zaire peace.

text.p: South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said on Monday this week's planned meeting between Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila could be the last chance to avoid a bloody showdown.
"The meeting on Wednesday may very well be the last chance to find a negotiated solution," he told reporters in Cape Town.

Mbeki, who has spearheaded South Africa's initiative for peace in Zaire, said he remained hopeful that Mobutu and Kabila would meet for the second time aboard a South African warship on Wednesday morning.
The two met for the first time aboard the South African navy ice-breaker Outeniqua on May 4 and agreed to meet again to discuss arrangements for a transition to democracy.
Rebel spokesmen said in Lubumbashi on Monday that Mobutu was running out of time and underlined Kabila's insistence that Wednesday's meeting would be his last with the ailing leader.
"The meeting with Mobutu on Wednesday will be the second and last one and let no one make a mistake about that," rebel information chief Raphael Ngenda told Reuters.

Mobutu, who is suffering from cancer, has ruled Zaire for 32 years and is alleged to have stripped the country of its wealth, but Kabila's rebels have seized control of three quarters of the country in a seven-month advance from the east.
Mbeki said he would probably travel to Zaire on Tuesday to hold separate meetings with Kabila in his Lubumbashi headquarters and with Mobutu in Kinshasa.
He identified the main issues as the composition of a transitional authority, a timetable for setting it up and the timing of Mobutu's resignation.
"We believe it's important that the basis should be laid for a resolution of these matters before we get to the meeting on Wednesday," he said.
"We are hopeful that it would be possible because if this agreement is not reached, it opens a way to a military solution being the only thing on the cards.
"We are hoping there will be sensitivity on both sides that it is better to enter an agreement than resolve it through the use of force," he said.

Mbeki said that in the next 48 hours South African mediators would hold intensive discussions with Kabila, Mobutu, U.N. envoy Mohamed Sahnoun and various countries with an interest in ending the conflict in Zaire.
He said Sahnoun had arrived in South Africa for talks on the issue.
